subject: general
question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 7 g/cm³ . Its internal and external radii are 1 cm and 2 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in grams) of the shell?

(Use pi = frac{22}7, and round off your answer to the nearest gram.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight = Volume × Density = [(4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)] × d

Weight = (4/3) × (22/7) × (2³ − 1³) × 7

Weight = (4/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 88/3 × 7 = 616/3 g

Weight ≈ 205.33 g

**∴ The correct answer is 205 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Density of metal = 7 g/cm³

External radius (R) = 2 cm

Internal radius (r) = 1 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hollow sphere = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Mass (Weight) = Volume × Density

 
 
 
• 
 R = 2 cm
 
• 
 r = 1 cm
 
 Hollow Spherical Shell Cross-Section

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (2³ − 1³)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (8 − 1)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 7 = 88/3 cm³

⇒ Weight = Volume × Density

⇒ Weight = (88/3) × 7 = 616/3 g

⇒ Weight = 205.33 g

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest gram gives 205 g.

**∴ The correct answer is 205 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Solid Sphere

The volume of a completely solid sphere is given by V = (4/3) × π × r³, where r is its constant outer radius.

Surface Area of a Hollow Sphere

The total surface area includes both the outer and inner surfaces, logically calculated as TSA = 4 × π × (R² + r²).

Mass and Volume Relationship

Density serves as the uniform ratio that connects the geometrical size of an object to its physical weight using Mass = Volume × Density.
